title: LogiConBench: Benchmarking Logical Consistencies of LLMs
claim: Existing benchmarks are saturated near ceiling, while ours stays hard; the task requires enumerating all consistent answers, which models often get wrong.
layout: 2 panels side by side; bar chart left, annotated truth-table example right
description: Two panels. Panel (a) is a grouped bar chart titled 'Accuracy of Frontier LLMs Across Logical Consistency Benchmarks'. It covers four models: gpt-5, grok-4-fast, gemini-2.5-pro and deepseek-r1-0528. Each model has five bars, with numeric labels above them. Four existing benchmarks (BeliefBank, EntailmentBank, LFC, Set-LConVQA/Set-SNLI) are drawn in blue and purple shades at 93–99%. The orange-red LogiConBench bar is much shorter, at 34, 12, 7.7 and 5.5, so it stands out. Panel (b) shows the enumerative task. A beige 'Question' box asks the model to enumerate all consistent Boolean label lists for three statements. Below it, a light-blue 'Answer' area has a truth table of three logical statements with T/F columns. The first two columns are highlighted yellow and green under 'Answered by the LLM', with a robot icon. Green check and red cross marks show which assignments are consistent. A bracket labeled 'All Possible Answers' sits under the table.
caption: (a) Accuracy of frontier LLMs on LogiConBench vs. existing benchmarks. Existing benchmarks are saturated, while LogiConBench remains challenging and discriminative. (b) Illustration of the enumerative task. Given three statements, the LLM must list all consistent label assignments, but often outputs incomplete or incorrect lists.
abstract: Logical consistency, the requirement that statements remain non-contradictory under logical rules, is fundamental for trustworthy reasoning, yet current LLMs often fail to maintain it even on simple inference tasks. Existing benchmarks for LLM logical consistency are not scalable, not diverse, and not challenging, with state-of-the-art models already surpassing 95\% accuracy. LogiConBench is the first benchmark that (1) generates unlimited logical rule combinations with precise labels, (2) provides controllable-depth graphs with explicit reasoning paths, and (3) remains challenging for state-of-the-art LLMs. To achieve this, LogiConBench automatically generates logical graphs where nodes represent symbolic propositions and edges denote reasoning relations. From these graphs, it samples lists of propositions, extracts reasoning paths, determines all consistent label lists, and translates them into diverse natural language expressions. While we release a 280K-sample corpus in this work, the framework can be scaled to generate unlimited data. To strengthen its evaluative significance, we evaluate 14 frontier LLMs on three tasks with varying difficulty levels, and find that the Enumerative task remains extremely challenging, with the best exact accuracy as only 34\%. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/Bellafc/LogiConBench.git.
